ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Ley 23 de 2015 and Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 2015: verification of identity and domicile of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs; mandatory screening against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Interpol notices, and Panama's national financial-blocking designations; enhanced due diligence mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates; ongoing transaction monitoring and five-year records retention required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Registro de Personas Jurídicas, official online portal https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa (Sistema de Reserva de Nombre en Línea)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin-script characters; Spanish is the official administrative language. A name may be in any language provided it is readable and pronounceable in Latin script and must end with a corporate suffix such as S.A., Corp., or Inc. The name must not be identical or phonetically similar to any existing registered entity and must not contain terms implying a regulated or governmental character absent prior ministerial authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written notice of denial from the Registro Público de Panamá, the applicant may file a reconsideración petition before the Dirección de Registro de Personas Jurídicas within five (5) business days of notification, and a subsequent apelación before the Director General within ten (10) business days, all under Ley 38 de 2000; alternatively, the applicant may file a fresh reservation request using a modified corporate name without appealing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only as the registered office address provided through a licensed Panamanian resident agent; the industrial quick-freezing production facility itself must be physically located on Panamanian territory and is not capable of virtual operation, as it requires a valid sanitary license and food-processing establishment registration from the Ministerio de Salud and the Autoridad Panameña de Seguridad de Alimentos.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 85% probability of an unannounced sanitary inspection within the first twelve (12) months of operation given the food manufacturing regime under the Reglamento General Técnico de Seguridad Alimentaria (Decreto Ejecutivo No. 532 de 2013), plus additional municipal inspections for the Aviso de Operación.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 32 of 1927 (General Law on Corporations, as amended) - Articles 1 to 4 on formation, Article 21 on capital, Article 39 on corporate powers; Executive Decree No. 5 of 2011 on electronic registry filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Departamento de Registro Mercantil (Mercantile Registry Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Publica de Constitucion (Pacto Social y Estatutos) - Public Deed of Incorporation and Corporate Bylaws
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama imposes no mandatory minimum paid-up capital; a nominal subscribed capital of US$10,000.00 divided into registered or bearer shares is customary. No escrow or initial deposit is required under Law 32 of 1927, and any contribution exceeding the capital account must be recorded in the share subscription ledger.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION 001/2025 - FIRST BOARD MEETING OF [CORPORATION] S.A. The Board unanimously resolves: (1) the subscription and issuance of 10,000 ordinary common shares to the initial subscribers, with the corporate secretary acknowledging receipt of subscription funds into the share premium account; (2) the registered office is fixed at the offices of the resident agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama; and (3) the officers are appointed as: Julio A. [Name], President; Maria L. [Name], Secretary-Treasurer; and the resident agent serves as legal representative for service of process. The Board authorizes the President and Secretary to execute all documents necessary to register this resolution with the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Oficina de Denominaciones (Name Office) / online via the Public Registry e-Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search application for the proposed corporate name in the Public Registry e-Platform or at the customer service window. Pay the search fee and obtain a non-binding availability certificate. Although Panama does not strictly require a name reservation, a thirty-day priority reservation is available upon request and should be obtained if the incorporation filing will be delayed. The certificate must be attached to the public deed.
required_dossiers: Identification document of the applicant or incorporator
Payment receipt for the name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity, amend the corporate name and resubmit; a written appeal may be filed before the Director General of the Registro Publico within five business days, or an alternative reserved name may be used in the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaria del Circuito de Panama (Notary of the Circuit of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the 'Pacto Social y Estatutos' setting out the corporate name, capital structure, corporate purpose (including industrial quick-freezing of steamed dim sum and dumplings), resident agent, and board membership. Have the incorporators or their attorney-in-fact appear before a Notary of the Circuit to execute the public deed. The notary will verify identity and collect the applicable stamp taxes. Notarization results in an 'Escritura Publica' that is then submitted to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos)
Legal identification or foreign passport of each incorporator
Power of attorney if an incorporator is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the draft for corrections, the parties must amend and re-execute the deed; any defect in the identity statements or capital structure is rectified before the notary assigns the protocol number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Departamento de Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized public deed to the Mercantile Registry together with the Form 004 registration request and evidence of payment of registry fees. Upon review, the Registry will issue the 'Inscripcion' (registration entry), and the corporation acquires legal personality as of that date. Obtain a certified copy known as 'Certificacion de Persona Juridica' for subsequent administrative and banking formalities.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed (Testimonio de la Escritura)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Registry may issue a 'nota de subsanacion' (observation). The applicant has ten business days to cure the defect by filing an amendment or supplementary document; otherwise the application is archived and must be resubmitted with corrected instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, register the corporation with the DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyentes). This is accomplished through the DGI online portal (Sede Electronica) or at the nearest DGI office. Submit the certified registry entry, the corporate bylaws, and the identification documents of the legal representative. Indicate the territorial tax regime applicable to the company. The DGI will issue the RUC certificate and the taxpayer identification number (NIT).
required_dossiers: Certificado de Inscripcion (certified registration from Public Registry)
Certified copy of the corporate bylaws
Resident agent certification of good standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries the submitted documents, the legal representative must upload the missing information via the e-Government portal; the RUC may be issued provisionally while the correction is completed within fifteen business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Books Opening and Statutory Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Departamento de Legalizaciones and the corporation's registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and legalize the corporate books required under Law 32 of 1927: the Share Register (Registro de Acciones), the Board Minutes Book, the Shareholders Minutes Book, and the General Ledger. Submit the books to the Public Registry for legalization, which consists of stamping and initialing each volume. These records must be maintained at the offices of the resident agent and must evidence all share subscriptions and board resolutions.
required_dossiers: Physical corporate book volumes (Shares ledger, minute books, and journal)
Certified copy of the registry inscription (Certificacion de Persona Juridica)
Appointment record of the legal representative and corporate officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the books are rejected for non-compliant binding, backdating, or missing pages, the company must obtain a corrected volume and resubmit for legalization; additional fees may apply for re-legalization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Direccion General de Industrias, in coordination with the relevant Municipal District Office issuing the Aviso de Operacion
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Alimentos (Food Sanitary Registration) and Municipal Aviso de Operacion (Business Operating Permit) for Industrial Frozen Food Manufacturing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Direccion de Evaluacion de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III - Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental) required for industrial frozen food processing facilities involving significant water consumption, refrigeration gases, and wastewater discharge; the environmental compliance plan must be approved before construction and operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must be pre-treated to achieve BOD5 no greater than 300 mg/L, COD no greater than 600 mg/L, TSS no greater than 200 mg/L, and pH between 6 and 9 before discharge into the municipal sewer system; grease traps and oil-water separators are mandatory. Refrigerant leaks must be prevented and reported in accordance with national ozone-depleting substance regulations. Cooking and steaming emissions shall be extracted and filtered to keep particulate matter and VOCs below permitted workplace thresholds. Solid food waste shall be stored in sealed, refrigerated containers and disposed of through licensed waste transporters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance is required through the 'Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios' issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama. Structural load and seismic inspections are to be approved by the Municipal Building Department. Occupational workplace clearance must be obtained from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), confirming compliance with industrial hygiene, ventilation, refrigeration safety, and occupational health requirements for food processing plants.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; taxpayer portal: Sistema de Facturación Electrónica and Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a resident legal agent, deliver apostilled constitutional documents and proof of a local registered address, and apply to the DGI for a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC). The RUC serves as the combined income tax and ITBMS registration identifier and is issued via DGI online offices or the TPV (Terminal de Punto de Venta) system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box pass-through election is available; a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima is taxed as a juridical person. Panama applies statutory territorial sourcing rules, so foreign-source income is generally excluded from tax. Hybrid mismatch elections are not applicable in the domestic ITBMS or income tax framework. A simplified small taxpayer regime is available for entities with low annual gross receipts.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold; all businesses carrying on taxable activities in Panama must register for ITBMS. A simplified small taxpayer regime applies to persons with annual gross receipts not exceeding B/. 300,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all registered taxpayers. Invoices must be issued through DGI-authorized emission systems, transmitted in XML format to the DGI's Factura Electrónica platform in real time, carry a digital signature, and include a QR quick-response code for validation and fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Panama to a foreign destination qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate. Offshore services rendered to non-residents and not used or consumed in Panamanian territory may also be zero-rated. The exporter must demonstrate the actual departure of goods from Panamanian customs territory and receipt of payment from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Mercancías de Exportación)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Depósito o Transferencia Bancaria del Exterior)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Misuse of export zero-rating constitutes tax evasion. Penalties include interest on underpaid tax, administrative fines of up to B/. 50,000, and surcharges of up to 200% of the omitted tax amount. Criminal prosecution under the Panamanian Tax and Criminal Codes is possible for fraudulent documentation. The DGI may retroactively claw back refunds for a statute-of-limitations period of at least five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No Panamanian central bank exists; Panama is fully dollarized under the Monetary Agreement with the United States. The de facto monetary policy is determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The domestic regulator with oversight of banking, foreign-exchange-related banking operations, and payment clearing is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas administers tax and legal-entity compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains full convertibility of the Balboa (PAB) at parity with the U.S. dollar, and the U.S. dollar itself is legal tender. There are no current-account or capital-account exchange controls, no prior approval for foreign direct investment, no restrictions on profit remittance, and no requirement to convert earnings into local currency. The only practical hurdles in remitting dividends or repatriating capital are standard corporate formalities, documentary banking checks, and applicable Panamanian tax rules, specifically the 10% dividend tax on distributions derived from Panama-source taxable profit and the absence of tax on foreign-source income. Banks will still require full source-of-funds documentation and updated beneficial ownership declarations before releasing funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement in Panama, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no time limit for repatriation of export receipts. Exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in U.S. dollars in any Panamanian or foreign banking account and may use them freely for operations, imports, dividends, or reinvestment. The only compliance obligation is to maintain clear commercial and customs records (invoice, bill of lading, packing list, customs declaration) and to ensure that proceeds flow into the same legal entity's bank account so that banking AML reviews and DGI territorial tax filings can be reconciled.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Commercial Letter of Credit Account / Trade Finance Account
Private Corporate Account / Cross-Border Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with legal limitations. Panama has no standalone 'electronic money institution' (EMI) license; overseas digital EMIs cannot take deposits or settle against the local clearing system without a licensed Panamanian bank or registered payment processor. A foreign EMI may be used as a virtual account and spend-management layer, but it is not deposit-insured in Panama and cannot issue Panamanian IBAN-equivalent rails. For this frozen dim sum factory, the treasury backbone should be licensed Panamanian bank accounts, with any EMI used only for non-core supplier disbursements or petty operational flows, never as the principal capital or sales-receipts repository.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally feasible for a Panama S.A. with a registered agent, using notarized and apostilled corporate documents, certified passport copies, and video-call KYC interviews with directors and ultimate beneficial owners. In practice, Tier-1 banks often require at least one physical visit by an authorized signer or legal representative before final account activation, especially for the first opening or if the company cannot provide a strong banking introduction. For ISIC 1074 frozen-food processing, the compliance risk is Low_Standard, so a one-day in-person documentary and signature session in Panama City is recommended to avoid delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership or use of bearer shares, nominee directors, or offshore 'shelf' structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry certification from Registro Público de Panamá, notarized share register showing fully registered shares, UBO declaration for every natural person holding over 10%, a written statement that no bearer shares are issued, sworn undertakings from directors that they are not nominees, certified copies of passports and proof of residence for all signatories, and a formal corporate structure chart with source-of-funds narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from an affiliate or foreign parent with no clear commercial or economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organizational charts, audited financial statements of the parent, loan or equity subscription agreements, board resolutions of both parties authorizing the capital transfer, bank statements showing the source account, copies of the receiving entity's tax identification documents, and a written capital deployment plan showing investment in factory equipment, inventory, and operating expenses for the dim sum manufacturing plant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade flows to higher-risk jurisdictions (e.g., China, Hong Kong, or regional counterparties) for machinery, ingredients, or packaging supplies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial sale and purchase contracts, purchase orders, commercial invoices, bill of lading and air-waybill records, customs export/import declarations, phytosanitary and food-processing certifications, shipping manifests, final beneficiary certificates, counterparty KYB files, denied-party screening reports, and a transaction rationale memo linking each disbursement to the factory's supply chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound U.S.-dollar capital injections should be routed by SWIFT MT103 to the Panama S.A.'s licensed operating or escrow account in Panama City. Although Panama imposes no exchange-control pre-approval or mandatory destination purpose code, the wire narrative must identify the economic substance, e.g., 'Capital contribution to Panama S.A. for frozen food factory project', and reference the notarized capital increase or share subscription resolution. The bank will verify the corporate name, Registered Public Registry filing, and source of funds. To ensure clean clearing, use a direct correspondent chain, avoid third-party consolidation accounts where possible, and ensure the ordering customer name matches the funding entity's KYB records. A KYC/AML file containing the funding agreement and board minutes should be delivered to the receiving bank before the wire is sent.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound settlement of imported machinery, raw materials, and packaging, use the SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments and advances, and commercial letters of credit (LCs) issued via SWIFT MT700 for larger or documentary trade transactions. Panamanian banks issue U.S.-dollar LCs and will accept bills of exchange, full set of clean-on-board bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, certificate of origin, and food-grade sanitary certificates as complying documents. For China-origin transactions, collections and LCs can also be routed through the bank's corresponding network in Hong Kong or Shanghai. Local clearing is via the Panamanian automated clearing house for domestic Balboa transactions, but cross-border trade should remain on SWIFT/MT-series rails for auditability and compliance traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in USD
USD/CNH deliverable forwards where corresponding liquidity is available
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CNH) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
FX options on USD/CNH and USD/EUR for risk containment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Franquicia) payment and declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by January 15 of each calendar year; DGI may grant short extension to January 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a fixed penalty of USD 500 plus default interest; persistent delinquency results in revenue lien, suspension of tax clearance, and eventual administrative strike-off from the Public Registry after continued non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 251 – Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayer, due no later than March 31 of the following tax year; DGI-approved extensions may move deadline to April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due (minimum USD 50, maximum USD 5,000) plus monthly default interest on unpaid tax; repeated failure triggers asset seizure, tax lien, and administrative strike-off risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before December 31 of each calendar year; any underlying change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change (no-change confirmation still required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing penalties start at USD 1,000; continued non-compliance leads to administrative suspension of corporate filings and possible deregistration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Companies with annual gross revenues or total assets exceeding USD 1,000,000 must file audited financial statements; banks, insurers, issuers of securities, and companies otherwise required by DGI are always subject to mandatory audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) as adopted by Panama; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for non-listed private companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Sociedad Anónima must keep a true and complete Beneficial Ownership Register and file an annual confirmation with the DGI through its resident agent; any transfer of shares or change in ultimate ownership must be notified to the agent and filed within 30 days, accompanied by a sworn declaration of current beneficial owners
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Share Transfers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 1,200 (typical annual resident-agent and registered-office professional fee range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 6,000 (typical audit fee range for a mid-sized food-processing S.A.)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial income tax system: only Panama-source profits are taxed, while foreign-source income that is not effectively connected with Panamanian operations is generally outside the taxable base. For a quick-freezing dim sum factory, there is no general manufacturing tax holiday, but Panama permits ordinary business deductions, accelerated depreciation on industrial production machinery, and a preferential treatment of reinvested profits in certain free-zone and export-processing regimes. If the plant is established under an industrial free-zone licence, qualifying export production may attract an income tax exemption or reduced effective rate; otherwise, the full 25% rate applies to taxable profits derived from manufacturing activities performed in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 105 – Declaración Jurada de Renta para Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) electronic tax portal (Sede Electrónica / e-Tax).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 31 March of the following fiscal year. Fiscal-year taxpayers may adopt a different annual period only with DGI prior authorization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the taxpayer’s 10-digit Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) number, legal name of the Sociedad Anónima, and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Panamanian S.A. owned by non-residents, the RUC is obtained through a resident fiscal representative or legal agent. The return must be signed by the legal representative with a valid Panama address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare gross income derived from all sources in Panama, including domestic and export sales of quick-frozen dim sum and dumplings, freight pass-through income, and any other operating revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panama-source revenue is taxable. If the factory sells to foreign distributors and the production takes place in Panama, the export sales are considered Panama-source income because the manufacturing activity occurs in Panamanian territory; gross receipts must be reported in local currency (balboas/USD).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim deductible operating expenses: raw material costs, industrial electricity, refrigeration and freezer-plant maintenance, wages and social security contributions, depreciation of machinery, freight and shipping costs, and interest on arm’s-length loans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by invoices legally issued in Panama or, for foreign suppliers, by commercial invoices with proof of payment through the banking system. Unsupported or non-documented related-party expenses are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the net taxable profit after subtracting allowable deductions from gross Panama-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should ensure the factory does not shift deductible profits abroad through excessive management fees. The net taxable profit is the base for computing the 25% corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the corporate income tax due at the 25% statutory rate on the net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the territorial adjustment: any foreign-source income not related to Panama activities may be excluded before application of the 25% rate, but only if it is properly documented and recorded separately in the accounting books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter advance income tax payments made during the year and any third-party withholding taxes credited against the final ISR liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident dividend or interest recipients may have had Panama withholding taxes withheld at source; such credits may be claimed only in the name of the Panama taxpayer, not the foreign beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Declaración de Transacciones con Partes Relacionadas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate whether the taxpayer engaged in transactions with foreign related parties in excess of the transfer-pricing documentation threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a factory with a foreign parent or related distributor, list related-party sales, royalty, management, and loan transactions. Failure to answer correctly is treated as a material omission and triggers TP review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties include a 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax, monthly interest at 1% or the applicable legal rate, and administrative fines ranging from PAB 50 to PAB 500 for minor filing defects. Intentional non-filing or fraudulent filing is treated as criminal tax evasion and can attract imprisonment from 2 to 5 years and fines up to PAB 25,000, in addition to reinstatement fees, inventory seizure, and cancellation of the factory’s operating licence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on gross dividends paid by a Panamanian S.A.; the rate is reduced to 5% when the profits distributed have been subject to, and effectively paid, the full 25% Panamanian corporate income tax at the company level. Dividends paid from profits that enjoyed an exemption or were taxable at a lower effective rate generally attract the 10% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a lower DTA withholding rate, the foreign shareholder must be the beneficial owner and a tax resident of a treaty jurisdiction. The protocol is: (i) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; (ii) arrange apostille or legalisation and, if required, a certified Spanish translation; (iii) submit the TRC and a treaty-benefit application to the Panamanian paying company before dividend distribution; (iv) the withholding agent files the application with the DGI and obtains a favourable resolution before applying the reduced rate. Panama applies the Principal Purpose Test and will deny treaty benefits where the transaction is structured mainly to obtain treaty relief. Full treaty relief is not automatic and cannot be claimed on the tax return without prior DGI approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For royalties paid by a Panamanian factory to a non-resident for the use of industrial technology, recipes, trademarks, or patents, the statutory withholding tax rate is 12.5% on gross royalty income. Interest paid to non-resident lenders on arm’s-length debt is subject to a 5% withholding tax on gross interest, although interest on loans from licensed foreign banks may be treated differently where Panama financial intermediation rules apply. Available DTA rates for interest usually range from 3% to 10%, and for royalties from 5% to 10%, depending on the treaty partner; Panama’s treaty network is limited and does not cover all export-market jurisdictions used for dim sum distribution.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taxpayers with related-party transactions exceeding PAB 2,500,000 (Panamanian balboas, equivalent to USD) or with annual gross revenue or assets above PAB 2,500,000 are generally required to maintain and submit Annual Transfer Pricing Documentation (Local File). Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting obligations apply where the multinational group has consolidated revenue equal to or above USD 850,000,000. The documentation threshold must be evaluated annually, and the DGI may issue a formal request for the Local File even below the quantitative thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama’s Economic Substance Regulations (Ley 254 de 2021) apply to mobile-income relevant activities, such as headquarters, distribution and service centres, financing and leasing, insurance, shipping, and holding of intangible assets. A quick-freezing dim sum and dumpling factory is an industrial manufacturer and therefore does not automatically fall within the ESR relevant-activity list. However, the Panamanian territorial tax regime requires real economic nexus for recognition of tax residence and source rules: the factory must maintain premises, refrigerated production equipment, employees, board minutes, bank accounts, and inventory records in Panama. A shell arrangement in which manufacturing is performed abroad while the S.A. merely issues invoices or holds funds will be re-characterised as Panama-source income and will violate DGI anti-avoidance doctrine and ESR if it conducts any relevant activity on the side.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of Panama-source revenue from Form 105, use of fictitious supplier invoices, under-reporting of quick-freezing production volumes, unreported cash sales, or forged deductions to push taxable profit below the 25% ISR liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion is punishable under Panamanian Penal Code Article 253/254 with imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and fines from PAB 10,000 to PAB 25,000. The DGI will also assess the omitted tax plus a 10% surcharge, monthly interest at 1%, and updated taxes. Goods, raw materials, factory equipment, and bank accounts may be seized as enforcement measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and accountants who sign or cause the filing of a false corporate return are personally jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. The corporate veil is pierced where the S.A. is used as an alter ego; directors face travel bans, asset freezes, and preventive detention during criminal proceedings, and may be personally ordered to make full civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Substance and Misclassification of Territorial Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Panamanian S.A. as a pure invoicing conduit while the actual dim sum factory, freezer assets, production equipment, personnel, and management decisions remain in another jurisdiction; quoting export sales as foreign-source income without local manufacturing substance; registering a shell company to avoid ISR on actual Panama-based production.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Panamanian Tax Code and Economic Substance Legislation, the DGI may reclassify the income as Panama-source, assess the 25% ISR plus a 20% penalty, and apply monthly interest. Administrative fines under the Economic Substance compliance regime can reach PAB 1,000,000 in serious cases; the Commercial Registry may strike off the entity, cancel licences, and impose a prohibition on holding corporate roles for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute sham transactions and sign declarations of foreign-source income despite no foreign presence become personally liable for the resultant tax deficiency. They are subject to civil restitution, disqualification from serving as directors in Panama, travel restrictions, and criminal prosecution for fraud where the sham is part of a larger asset-protection or money-laundering scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Violations / Disguised Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling quick-frozen dim sum to a related Hong Kong or US distributor at artificially low intercompany prices; paying excessive management, royalty, or technical-service fees to the foreign parent; providing undocumented loans with high interest rates to foreign shareholders; failing to maintain Local File documentation when related-party transactions exceed PAB 2,500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI will make a transfer-pricing adjustment using an approved arm’s-length method, assess 25% ISR on the adjusted Panama-source profit, add a 20% penalty on the omitted tax and 1% monthly interest, and may impose secondary adjustments to reflect the recharacterised distribution. Interest deductions on excessive shareholder debt are disallowed to the extent the loan is not at arm’s length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who sign TP documentation, approve loans, or issue related-party invoices knowing them to be non-arm’s-length are jointly liable for the adjusted assessment. The court may pierce the corporate veil and order directors to repay the shortfall, impose travel bans pending collection, and refer the case to criminal prosecution for fraudulent misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Trade-Based Money Laundering Through Export Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using SWIFT letters of credit and TT wires to over-invoice or under-invoice dim sum exports, routing payments through Panama exchange houses or shell accounts, splitting large freezing-plant contracts to avoid compliance thresholds, or failing to identify ultimate beneficial owners and KYC documentation for international counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 and the Panamanian Penal Code, trade-based money laundering is punishable with imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and fines of 5 to 10 times the value of the illicit transaction. The Superintendencia de Bancos and the Financial Intelligence Unit may impose administrative fines up to PAB 1,000,000 on the corporate entity, freeze bank accounts, seize export shipments, and initiate in rem forfeiture of the production plant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who approve suspicious wire transfers, sign false commercial invoices, or fail to maintain an AML compliance programme for export payments are individually criminally liable. They face personal arrest and travel bans during investigation, asset freezes on personal and corporate accounts, disqualification from banking roles, and personal civil restitution for funds laundered through the corporate entity.
